fix.explain: Your forearm rolled 165° through contact (measured by the wrist sensor). ASSUMED: the racket face turns 0.3° per degree of roll above the forehand's good median (136.8°), so your face was 8.5° closed, towards the left wall (cross-court) and your PREDICTED ball goes cross-court: hits the tin. The ghost rolls its forearm 28.2° less through contact (165° → 136.8°), so its face is square and its PREDICTED ball goes straight down the right wall: hits the tin. Ball speed 43.8 → 43.8 km/h, ESTIMATE (sensor). ASSUMED: the 12° launch angle and the spot on court.

Aim: your stated straight drive, turned cross-court by the racket face, which is assumed to turn 0.3° per degree of forearm roll from the wrist sensor above the good median (capped at 15°); the camera can't see the face.
